newsitem.title: USA: Distant CME pork bellies end limit up, August down.
newsitem.headline: Distant CME pork bellies end limit up, August down.

text.p: February and March CME pork belly futures closed up the daily 3.000-cent-per-lb limit while the soon-to-be-spot August finished lower along with nearby hog futures contracts, traders said.

Pork bellies closed 0.750 cent per lb lower to up the 3.000-cent limit with only August off at 83.200 cents abd February 1998 bellies up 3.000 cents at 75.150 cents. Hog futures ended mixed, from 0.675 cent a lb lower to 0.250 higher with August off most at 81.350 cents.
Rolling of long August positions into next year contracts on concern over deliveries started the runup in deferred bellies with fund buying and stops taking prices up the limit late, traders said.
"There's obviously a lot of rolling today because you have first notice day coming up Monday," said Dale Benson, vice president and senior livestock analyst for Dean Witter.
He said the incentive to sell August came on concern that part of the deliverable supply was of low-grade bellies that are more suitable for the trimmings market.
A strong cash belly market, as packers cut hog kill rates, and a larger-than-expected out-movement in the CME out-of-town report limited selling pressure in August, they said.
CME on Tuesday reported a net out-movement of 3.467 million lbs, above the high end of trade estimates.
